overview: This event ties together hydraulic system, spin, and ocf recovery procedures in a way that should already make sense before you step. You should be ready to brief what changes the plan, what numbers matter, and where the usual errors start once the workload climbs.

items.text: OCF Recovery Procedures is judged by how well you enter it, stay ahead of the aircraft, and recover without needing cleanup coaching.

children.text: Know the entry airspeed, altitude, configuration, and cockpit setup before you start the maneuver.
OCF Recovery Procedures is judged by how well you enter it, stay ahead of the aircraft, and recover without needing cleanup coaching.
Know the entry airspeed, altitude, configuration, and cockpit setup before you start the maneuver.
Advance PCL to MAX
Set flaps from LDG → TO
At ≥110 KIAS, raise flaps
A torque setting above 60% in the stall can induce a left torque roll. Full right rudder and aileron may not prevent departure. Be especially cautious during power-on turning stalls.
If in a low energy state with AOA <18.0 and airspeed too low to sustain level flight, apply power cautiously. If in an unrecoverable descent, EJECT if below 6000’ AGL.
Stick shaker typically activates at 15.5 units AOA, which corresponds to 5–10 KIAS above stall in unaccelerated flight.

(N) Oil pressure may drop below 40 psi during idle-power spins; this is acceptable if no limits are exceeded and normal pressure returns after recovery.

items.text: land into XW using wing-low method, touch down on upwind gear first; waveoff if side motion, drift, or crab occurs

Keep upwind wing down, do not level wings
Use rudder to align nose with runway
Increase aileron input as speed decreases
Use rudder/brakes to stay straight; brakes below 80 KIAS
PCL - MAX, rotate at 90 KIAS
The usual trap is missing the setup picture, then trying to salvage Crosswind Takeoffs/Touch-and-Goes/Full-Stop Landings late.
